correctness.rationale: The finite classification was independently replayed from the definition. Exactly 352 of the 512 binary 3-by-3 matrices have split characteristic polynomial. Enumerating every reduced-row-echelon basis gives all 788035 six-dimensional subspaces and finds exactly 35 in which all 64 matrices are triangularizable; enumerating all 43435 seven-dimensional subspaces finds none. A separate exact conjugation replay over all 168 elements of \(\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb F_2)\) partitions those 35 spaces into orbits of sizes \(21,7,7\), matching the three displayed representatives. This establishes both maximality and exhaustive similarity classification independently of the saved certificate.

originality.rationale: Originality passes. The complete open HTML of the 2026 characteristic-two paper was inspected. It explicitly identifies classification of optimal weakly triangularizable spaces as a remaining problem and says the methods for larger perfect characteristic-two fields fail for the field of two elements and require a different approach. The known dimension formula already covers \((\mathbb F_2,n=3)\) because the previously possible exception was only fields with cardinality strictly less than \(n-1\), but the larger-field structural classification does not cover this binary case. Fresh Resultary search found only the audited classification and adjacent binary matrix-space problems, not a prior 35-space/three-orbit theorem.
residual_risks: An unindexed older finite-geometry computation of the same 35 spaces could exist; no such classification was found.
